newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends weaker, recovers some early losses.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends weaker, recovers some early losses.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended softer on Tuesday from Monday's close, but partly rebounded from opening weakness on Tuesday after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan raised expectations that Canadian and U.S. interest rates would hold steady * Canada unit seen trading between C$1.3775 and C$1.3805 overnight.
The Canadian dollar ended softer on Tuesday compared to Monday's close, but recovered some early losses after comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The unit finished around C$1.3785 (US$0.7254), versus Monday's close of C$1.3772 (US$0.7261), but stronger than opening levels of C$1.3804 (US$0.7244) on Tuesday.
"Greenspan had a good effect on the Canadian dollar as it did for the bonds and the stock market. But fundamentally there isn't a big change," one currency trader said.
Speculation that Greenspan might deliver a hawkish message to the House Banking subcommittee on the first leg of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony hurt the Canadian dollar earlier today.
But Greenspan said there was no need to raise interest rates because U.S. economic growth was slowing.
"I have no doubt that the current stance of policy...will need to be changed at some point, Greenspan said. "For the present, demand growth does appear to have moderated."
Canadian bonds and stocks also rallied on Tuesday with the Toronto Stock Eschange key 300 Index rising more than one percent.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose against the German mark to 1.3222 marks from 1.3044 marks at Monday's close. The unit rose to 83.45 yen from 84.34 yen.
